"With most refugees dispossessed, having lost homes, possessions and often loved ones and displaced for upwards of 20 years, they represent a significant source of population disquility," said the study. "Solving the refugee crisis in the US$6tn 20 largest economies of the world could involve a total annual financing of US$17.5bn (or 0.012 per cent of these country's GDPs)," it added.
